response_text: A system call is a software-generated interrupt that is intentionally generated by a user program request in which the Operating System, OS, takes over in order to perform a task that requires privileged access or kernel-level functionality. This allows a user-mode program to interact with system resources such as files, devices, and other processes. In terms of its role in program structure, it is a gateway operation that through which applications ask the OS to perform operations that they can not that include resource management, process management, and system information. Moreover, it provides a transition from user mode to kernel mode, and it forms a crucial abstraction layer that shields used program from complexity and hardware specific details of the system. System calls are also synchronous in that they wait for the kernel to complete operation before returning control to the user program. It is important to note that system calls enforce security boundaries, as they are the only way that user mode code accesses and manipulates system resources. Without this protection, malicious programs could access or corrupt other programs, programs would not be isolated from one another, the kernel memory and critical data structures would be at risk to manipulation, and programs could bypass system-wide policies.\n
